summary: APS opposes sunsetting E-Rate and emphasizes the ongoing need for connectivity in its network infrastructure. APS urges the Commission not to assume that schools have completed their internal networks or that current Category Two budgets are more than applicants need. APS does not operate a gold-plated network. It operates a large network serving schools, administrative facilities, students, employees, instructional systems, safety functions, and thousands of connected devices. APS’s own Category Two record shows the continuing need. In the first year of the FY2026–2030 cycle, APS has requested approxim APS supports strong oversight of E-Rate and sensible protections for the Universal Service Fund. It also encourages the Commission to build on what has worked. Do not sunset a program that continues to support essential school infrastructure. Preserve competition and applicant choice. Keep Category Two support grounded in the real cost of maintaining networks. Recognize cybersecurity as part of reliable connectivity.
